posts.headline: The S&P 500 just fell into a correction and the Nasdaq went negative for 2026 — and that's the index sitting inside most 401(k)s.
posts.source: Source: Associated Press market close, Nov. 20, 2026
posts.caption:
Wall Street just closed its worst week in more than a year — and if you own an index fund, a 401(k) or an RRSP, this one lands on you.

The S&P 500 fell 3.7% Friday (down 265 points to 6,910) and is now in a 'correction' — more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record. The Nasdaq slid 5.3%, erasing its entire 2026 gain and turning negative for the year. The Dow dropped 1.9%, about 950 points, to 48,147 (Associated Press, Nov. 20).

Why it matters even if you never watch the market: the S&P 500 is the backbone of most target-date funds and 401(k)s on both sides of the border, so a 3.7% day trims the balance millions are saving on. Nvidia — a top holding in many of those funds — fell another 13.8%.

My take: a seven-day losing streak, the longest since 2020, is unnerving — but a retirement account is scored on the day you retire, not the day the headlines are worst.

Has this week pushed you to check your 401(k) or RRSP?
